reasoning_content.head: The user reports broken emotion appraisal in the Harmonicity simulation and wants a root cause diagnosis from logs. I need to find where appraisals are logged and compare recent vs old runs. First check grep_log for "appraisal" across all buckets to locate relevant log lines; then probe_llm with varying max_tokens because truncation is a common silent failure mode in LLM-based systems, and get_llm

The failure spikes at tick 7500 and collapses to near-zero after 8000 — that's a hard break, not gradual decay. The parse fails because the LLM output is truncated mid-generation, so grep_llm for "finish_reason: length" in those buckets will confirm truncation as the mechanism before I blame context/max_tokens.

The grep returned the same parse-failure buckets — no 'length' lines in any of them. So it's not a simple max_tokens cut; something else is mangling the output or dropping generations entirely after tick 7500. Check get_llm_server_props to see if context/slots were changed and probe_llm with varying max_tokens as a diagnostic cross-check for truncation regardless of what grep found.

Gemma-4 26B with ctx=8k and n_ctx_per_slot=2048 means each of the 4 parallel slots gets only ~2kb context — that's tiny for an appraisal prompt. The failure at tick 7500 is likely a slot being overloaded or the prompt growing past 2048 tokens. Probe with different max_tokens to isolate whether truncation is indeed the driver and confirm it's not just a bad system prompt.

Smoking gun: reasoning alone is ~4k tokens and content len is 0 at max=512/1536 — the model spends its entire budget on internal chain-of-thought before emitting a single output token. That's why parsing fails; there IS no completion, only invisible CoT. The fix: raise n_ctx_per_slot so reasoning doesn't cannibalize the generation window.

Grep returned the parse-failure buckets again — no n_ctx line in any of them. So there's NO server config log to blame; it must be a hardcoded limit or an upstream override I haven't seen yet. Let me grep for 'n_ctx=' anywhere else, and also check the system prompt itself for any max-token cap that would force this truncation.

Still the parse-failure buckets — no n_ctx line anywhere in them either. That's bizarre; it means there is NO log entry for n_ctx at all, which points to a hardcoded limit I can't find via grep of these lines. Let me read the actual system prompt file directly to see if max_tokens or any other constraint is set there instead of in a config line.
